input: DTC: P0301 | System: Powertrain | Fault family: misfire_single_cylinder | Description: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected | Ranked fix #1: Swap spark plug and ignition coil to confirm the cylinder

output.diagnosis: Code P0301 (Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected) sets when the ECM's misfire monitor isolates repeated combustion events lost on one specific cylinder (or, for the unspecified variant, a single cylinder it cannot pin down). The diagnosis path is identical regardless of which cylinder number is reported: the fault lives in that cylinder's ignition, fuel delivery, or mechanical sealing, most commonly a fouled spark plug or failing coil, a clogged or leaking injector, or low compression from a burnt valve or worn rings.
parts: Swap spark plug and ignition coil to confirm the cylinder
repair_steps: 1. Remove the coil and plug from the misfiring cylinder
2. Inspect the plug for fouling, wear, or an incorrect gap
3. Swap the coil with a known-good adjacent cylinder's coil
4. Clear the code and see if the misfire follows the coil or stays with the cylinder
5. Replace the plug and/or coil based on the result
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P0301 (Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

instruction: Diagnose this OBD-II trouble code for a second-hand vehicle inspection and produce a structured repair plan JSON.
input: DTC: P0456 | System: Powertrain | Fault family: evap_small_leak | Description: EVAP System Leak Detected (very small leak) | Ranked fix #3: Replace EVAP purge solenoid valve

output.diagnosis: Code P0456 (EVAP System Leak Detected (very small leak)) sets when the EVAP leak-detection monitor cannot hold vacuum or pressure in the fuel vapor system within its small-leak threshold (typically a 0.020 in. equivalent orifice), including the tighter very-small-leak threshold and the fuel-tank-side/fresh-air-side variants used on natural-vacuum leak detection systems, or when the general EVAP system monitor itself fails. The dominant causes are a loose or worn fuel filler cap, a cracked EVAP hose, or a purge/vent solenoid that no longer seals.
repair_steps: 1. Locate the purge solenoid on the engine-side EVAP line
2. Verify it holds vacuum when de-energized with a hand pump
3. Replace the solenoid and clip the harness
4. Clear the code and re-run the EVAP monitor
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P0456 (EVAP System Leak Detected (very small leak)) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

input: DTC: P0102 | System: Powertrain | Fault family: maf_circuit | Description: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit Low | Ranked fix #1: Clean MAF sensing element and inspect intake ducting

output.diagnosis: Code P0102 (Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit Low) sets when the ECM detects an implausible signal from the mass air flow sensor — reported airflow disagrees with throttle position and engine speed, or the signal voltage leaves its calibrated window. The most common physical causes are a contaminated MAF sensing element, unmetered air entering the intake downstream of the sensor, and chafed or corroded wiring in the sensor's 5V reference / signal-return circuit.
parts: Clean MAF sensing element and inspect intake ducting
repair_steps: 1. Remove the intake duct clamp and unplug the MAF connector
2. Remove the sensor with a security Torx bit
3. Spray the hot-wire element with dedicated MAF cleaner (never touch it)
4. Inspect the duct for cracks or loose clamps downstream of the sensor
5. Reinstall, clear the code, and road test
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P0102 (Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit Low) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

instruction: Diagnose this OBD-II trouble code for a second-hand vehicle inspection and produce a structured repair plan JSON.
input: DTC: P0441 | System: Powertrain | Fault family: evap_purge_flow_performance | Description: EVAP System Incorrect Purge Flow | Ranked fix #1: Inspect the purge line for kinks, collapse, or restriction

output.diagnosis: Code P0441 (EVAP System Incorrect Purge Flow) sets when the ECM commands EVAP purge and the resulting flow through the purge line — measured by fuel trim shift, a purge flow sensor, or line pressure — is significantly higher or lower than expected for the commanded duty cycle, including the high-load purge line performance variant used on turbocharged/boosted platforms. Causes are a partially clogged purge line or canister restricting flow, a purge solenoid that leaks or does not open fully, or a collapsed/pinched purge hose under vacuum.
parts: Inspect the purge line for kinks, collapse, or restriction
repair_steps: 1. Trace the purge line from the canister to the intake/throttle body
2. Look for a kinked, collapsed, or pinched section, especially near heat sources
3. Replace the damaged hose section
4. Clear the code and monitor purge flow on a scan tool
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P0441 (EVAP System Incorrect Purge Flow) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

input: DTC: P0505 | System: Powertrain | Fault family: idle_air_control_system | Description: Idle Control System | Ranked fix #1: Clean throttle body and IAC passage

output.diagnosis: Code P0505 (Idle Control System) sets when commanded idle RPM (or, on diesel platforms, idle fuel quantity) does not match the ECM's target, or the idle air control actuator's circuit reports an open/out-of-range condition. Root causes are a carbon-fouled IAC valve or throttle bore restricting airflow, an unmetered vacuum/intake air leak that pushes idle high, a sticking throttle plate, or a failed IAC motor/solenoid and its wiring.

repair_steps: 1. Remove the intake duct and IAC valve or throttle body cover
2. Spray throttle-body cleaner into the idle air passage and throttle bore
3. Wipe away carbon with a shop towel, avoiding the throttle plate seal edge
4. Reinstall, reset idle relearn, and confirm idle stabilizes
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P0505 (Idle Control System) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

input: DTC: P0301 | System: Powertrain | Fault family: misfire_single_cylinder | Description: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected | Ranked fix #3: Run a cylinder compression or leak-down test

output.diagnosis: Code P0301 (Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected) sets when the ECM's misfire monitor isolates repeated combustion events lost on one specific cylinder (or, for the unspecified variant, a single cylinder it cannot pin down). 2. Compare the flagged cylinder's reading against its neighbors
3. Add oil and retest (wet test) to isolate rings vs. valves
4. Follow up with a leak-down test to confirm the exact leak path

input: DTC: P1259 | System: Powertrain | Fault family: honda_vtec_system_circuit | Description: VTEC System Malfunction Rear Bank 1 | Ranked fix #2: Test the VTEC oil pressure switch

output.diagnosis: Code P1259 (VTEC System Malfunction Rear Bank 1) sets when the ECM does not see the VTEC oil pressure switch confirm a cam-profile shift after commanding the VTEC spool valve solenoid, or detects an open/shorted condition on either component's circuit. VTEC (Variable valve Timing and lift Electronic Control) uses oil pressure routed through the spool valve to lock a pin between rocker arms for the high-lift cam lobe; the pressure switch confirms that pressure actually built before the ECM trusts the engagement. Low or degraded engine oil that cannot build switching pressure, a clogged VTEC oil strainer screen starving the spool valve, a failed pressure switch, or a spool valve solenoid with a sticking or shorted coil are the common causes.
parts: Test the VTEC oil pressure switch
repair_steps: 1. Locate the VTEC oil pressure switch on the cylinder head
2. Back-probe the switch connector and confirm it opens/closes with engine oil pressure
3. Replace the switch if it stays open or closed regardless of pressure
4. Clear the code and confirm the switch now toggles during a test drive
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P1259 (VTEC System Malfunction Rear Bank 1) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

output.diagnosis: Code P0303 (Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected) sets when the ECM's misfire monitor isolates repeated combustion events lost on one specific cylinder (or, for the unspecified variant, a single cylinder it cannot pin down). The diagnosis path is identical regardless of which cylinder number is reported: the fault lives in that cylinder's ignition, fuel delivery, or mechanical sealing, most commonly a fouled spark plug or failing coil, a clogged or leaking injector, or low compression from a burnt valve or worn rings.
parts: Test and clean or replace the cylinder's fuel injector

2. Swap the injector with a neighboring cylinder to see if the misfire follows
3. Clean the injector on an ultrasonic bench or replace it
4. Reinstall with new O-rings and clear codes
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P0303 (Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

4. Confirm clean square-wave signals on a scope

VTEC (Variable valve Timing and lift Electronic Control) uses oil pressure routed through the spool valve to lock a pin between rocker arms for the high-lift cam lobe; the pressure switch confirms that pressure actually built before the ECM trusts the engagement. parts: Clean the VTEC oil strainer and test the spool valve solenoid
repair_steps: 1. Remove the spool valve assembly and its inline oil strainer screen
2. Clean or replace a screen clogged with sludge or metal debris
3. Measure spool valve solenoid coil resistance against the factory specification
4. Command the solenoid with a scan tool and confirm it clicks and moves freely
5. Reinstall with a new gasket and road-test for clean VTEC engagement
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC P1259 (VTEC System Malfunction Rear Bank 1) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.

3. Install the new sensor with a fresh O-ring seated fully
4. Clear the code and confirm speedometer/cruise operation on a test drive

instruction: Diagnose this OBD-II trouble code for a second-hand vehicle inspection and produce a structured repair plan JSON.
input: DTC: C0031 | System: Chassis | Fault family: wheel_speed_sensor_circuit | Description: Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor | Ranked fix #4: Repair chafed wheel speed sensor harness wiring

output.diagnosis: Code C0031 (Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor) sets when the ABS module loses a valid electrical signal from a wheel speed sensor -- the circuit reads open, shorted low or high, drops out intermittently, fails to correlate with the other three wheels, or reports an incorrect component installed. The diagnosis and repair are identical at every corner: a corroded or unplugged connector, a chafed harness conductor rubbing on the strut or subframe, or a failed Hall-effect/variable-reluctance sensor element. This is distinct from a tone-ring or mechanical fault, where the wiring and sensor test fine but the signal is noisy or absent because of physical damage at the reluctor wheel.
parts: Repair chafed wheel speed sensor harness wiring
repair_steps: Trace the harness from the sensor to the body connector along the strut and control arm
Identify the chafe point, commonly where the harness crosses suspension travel
Repair damaged conductors with solder and heat-shrink, then re-route and secure the harness
Clear codes and confirm all four corners correlate correctly on a road test
output.buyer_advice: For a used-car purchase: ask seller for proof that DTC C0031 (Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor) was repaired and codes cleared after a drive cycle.
